name: Restaurants
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For restaurant, cafe and dining-business owners. Explore phone orders, reservations, menu questions and service interruptions. Match the actual need instead of defaulting to private-event inquiries. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: What kinds of calls interrupt service most often?
How do phone orders reach your kitchen today?
Would you need pickup orders, delivery orders, or both?
Which ordering or POS system do you use?
What menu choices, modifiers and order changes should she confirm?
What should happen if the order cannot reach the agreed destination?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved questions about hours, location, parking, and published dining arrangements.
Capture an event inquiry's contact details, requested date, party size, and reason for calling without confirming availability.
Collect a reservation-related callback request and send its summary to ONE agreed destination for staff review.
levels.probe: Would a clear callback message solve most missed calls, or do guests usually need a staff decision immediately?
fit_signals: Staff can return calls and make all reservation decisions themselves.
Most missed calls concern approved information or straightforward inquiries.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Take and read back a food order using the approved menu, sizes, modifiers and availability; capture pickup or delivery details and pass the order to the agreed destination through the configured workflow.
Book or change eligible reservations, qualify event inquiries and update approved customer records through verified systems and restaurant rules.
Offer screened transfers when requested or when staff judgment is needed; if staff are busy, use the agreed order-taking or follow-up workflow.
levels.probe: How do phone orders reach your kitchen today?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Gather a detailed service complaint, relevant visit context, and requested resolution for the human manager.
Explain approved reservation or cancellation policies and escalate requests requiring an exception.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: Level 1 includes no booking, screened transfer, or CRM integration; message capture is not a confirmed reservation.
Do not handle payments, guarantee allergen safety, provide medical advice, or make unapproved dietary assurances. Route food-safety and ingredient concerns to restaurant staff.
Staff confirm menus, policies, availability, and services. Humans decide refunds, discounts, credits, and policy exceptions.
Use the shared phone-agent pricing source for fees and terms. Do not duplicate prices or present a proposal as an active Jaylene capability.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.

Food-order taking and readback fit Level 2. Direct Toast/POS submission must be verified; taking details is not successful submission. Payment collection is a distinct capability and must not be promised or requested in this sales call. Never guarantee allergen safety or availability from memory.
setup_requirements: Approve current FAQs and identify who maintains hours, menus, and policies.
Choose intake fields and ONE summary destination; collect only necessary details.
Define staff routing, acceptance rules, unavailable-staff fallbacks, and complaint escalation.
Verify actual software compatibility and distinguish consultation booking from restaurant reservations.
Test the agreed call paths before launch; never promise bookings, transfers, or messages without confirmed execution.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.example: A separately scoped website could clarify menus, hours, and the inquiry path.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: I run a restaurant. Food-order calls interrupt service.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Level 2 could take those orders and pass them along, with the supporting automation included. How do phone orders reach your kitchen today?

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: We use Toast. Can she take the order instead of transferring it?

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Yes, order-taking belongs in Level 2. We would confirm whether we can submit directly into Toast during setup. Would you need pickup orders, delivery orders, or both?

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: Pickup, and I do not want an extra automation charge.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: The automation for the agreed receptionist duties is included in Level 2. We still need to verify the Toast connection. What menu choices or modifiers should she confirm?
